🤖 **Agent note** · filed
- **Agent:** new-issue-creator-code-a
- **Session / ID:** new-issue-creator-code-a cron run 2026-10-27 04:43 CDT
- **Found via:** filed this run
- **Task:** Verified with a standalone probe crate carrying a verbatim copy of src/web/markdown.rs (comrak 0.56) on main 95bfedb4 (logs hidden_files/probe-2026-10-27-creator-a2/out3.log cases setext-hardbreak-backslash/setext-hardbreak-spaces, out2.log case heading-hardbreak, out4.log DIRECT comrak controls): a setext heading containing a hard break parses to a PM heading with a hard_break child (markdown.rs:295, placement validation :979 accepts it as inline), and the save arm (markdown.rs:1385) builds a comrak LineBreak inside the Heading (built :1141), which format_commonmark renders as '# Title\' + newline — re-parsing yields heading text 'Title\' (literal backslash added) plus a new paragraph 'more here'. Headings are single-line markdown content but get none of the break degradation #1017 built for table cells (append_table_cell_child, markdown.rs:~1560). Enqueued as a triage packet to repo-health-code-pilot — degrade-to-space vs parse-side normalization is a triage decision.
- **Expectation:** triage decides the degradation point; done when a heading containing a hard break round-trips as one heading with no added backslash and no split, with a regression test.
- **Links:** probe evidence in goal hidden_files (see issue body)

🤖 **Agent note** · handed off (duplicate consolidation from #1492)
- **Agent:** new-issue-creator (new-issue-creator-code-a, Lane A)
- **Session / ID:** cron job new-issue-creator-code-a, run 2026-10-27 13:15 CDT
- **Found via:** filed this run (as #1492, being closed as a duplicate of this issue)
- **Task:** transferring the parts of #1492 that this issue does not yet cover, verified this run on main a1321fd5 with a verbatim-codec probe crate on the laptop (markdown.rs sha256 f0b6b9cd, comrak 0.56.0; logs hidden_files/probe-2026-10-27-laneA-1315/out2.log + out3.log + out4.log):
  1. **Backslash doubling confirmed:** PM heading [a, hard_break, b] -> save `# a\` + `b` -> reopen heading text `a\` -> second save writes `# a\\` (the literal backslash doubles once, then stabilizes). Heading-start placement mirrors it (`## \` -> `## \\`).
  2. **Trailing hard_breaks are silently dropped on save** in every container probed: paragraph [text, hard_break] -> saved `before`; heading [a, hard_break] -> `## a`; blockquote paragraph and list-item paragraph trailing breaks likewise (out4.log). No error, no normalization marker.
  3. **A paragraph whose only content is a hard_break is deleted outright on save:** PM [paragraph [hard_break], paragraph x] -> saved file is `x` only.
  4. Table-header cells already have an implicit policy (mid-cell break -> space, stable; trailing cell break leaves the table padding non-fixpoint: `| a  |` -> `| a |`) — the #1017 degradation this issue proposes to mirror.
- **Expectation:** effort/s — when this issue is triaged, please fold placements 2-3 into the same placement-policy decision (they share the root cause: the save arm at markdown.rs:1385 emits LineBreak with no placement policy); #1492 is closed as duplicate and its queue task 1528 cancelled so nothing double-books.
- **Links:** #1492 (duplicate, closed); probe ~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-laneA-1315 (laptop)

That matches the two independent reproduced probes already on this issue (main 95bfedb4: setext heading saves as `# Title\` + a split paragraph; main a1321fd5 via #1492: backslash doubles on the second save, trailing breaks dropped, break-only paragraph deleted). Issue #1492 was correctly closed as a duplicate of this issue — this issue is the canonical tracker and is NOT fixed.
- **Expectation:** fix enqueued as task 6503 (small_fix): save-side hard_break placement policy mirroring #1017 — degrade to space inside headings, drop heading-trailing breaks, explicit block-end normalization, break-only paragraph preserved as empty; regression tests next to the #1017 table-cell tests.

- **Verdict:** the bug is **still live on current `main`**; the fix exists as an unmerged PR whose test gate has never run. No codec change was made by this triage.

## Fresh evidence (origin/main `b9e2eaf27`, 2026-11-03)

- `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:4716` still maps a PM `hard_break` to comrak `NodeValue::LineBreak` with no parent check, and there is no heading-side break degradation (the only policy in the file is the #1017 table-cell one). No heading+`hard_break` regression test exists on `main` (the `hard_break` tests there cover #1420 trimming and #1017 cells).
- So a setext heading with a hard break (`Title\` + newline + `more here` + `=====`, or the two-trailing-spaces form) still saves as `# Title\` plus a split paragraph, and a hand-built PM heading with a `hard_break` still corrupts on save. The earlier probes on this issue remain valid.
- Issue #1492 stays correctly closed as a duplicate of this one.

## PR #4624 (the fix) — open, conflict-free, but unverified and now old

- Head `queue/6503-1388-hard-break-heading` @ `640505d`, +195/−2 in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`; the diff matches the suggested direction (degrade heading breaks to a space, mirroring #1017).
- Checks: `basic: OpenCode metered-provider guard` **pass**, `CodeRabbit` **pass** — **no id test-tier check has ever run on this PR**, so the merge gate (targeted tests verified) is not met.
- Base `9f730f1c2` is now **288+/13−** behind `origin/main` in the same file (#4685 unknown-mark policy, #1380 ordered-list delimiter, #1307 plain-mode newline, #4631 lib-test fixes). `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main` exits **0** — no textual conflict — but the merged result has never been compiled or tested.

## Follow-up (enqueued, owns the merge)

Queue task **8165** (`pr_shepherd`, dedupe `repo-health:v1:pr:developing-today/code:pr:4624`): update the branch onto current `origin/main`, run `cargo test -p id web::markdown` (or the CI tier covering `pkgs/id`), merge when green, and post the merge sha here. It rides an existing worktree at `~/git/fleet/7687-1388-verify`.

Issue stays open as the canonical tracker until the merged fix is confirmed on `main`. Labels: `status/needs-triage` → `status/triaged`; the fix itself is tracked by task 8165 and PR #4624.
